keyVerseText: Thou shalt bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of thine inheritance, in the place, O LORD, which thou hast made for thee to dwell in, in the Sanctuary, O Lord, which thy hands have established.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun מִקְדָּשׁ (miqdâsh) derives from the root קָדַשׁ (qâdash), which fundamentally means to consecrate, sanctify, or set apart as holy. This root conveys the idea of making something ceremonially or morally clean, dedicated for a sacred purpose. Thus, מִקְדָּשׁ literally signifies a place or thing that has been set apart or hallowed, emphasizing its consecrated status beyond just a generic 'holy place.'
usageInScripture: The word מִקְדָּשׁ appears 74 times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently translated as sanctuary, holy place, or a consecrated space. It refers primarily to Israel's sacred sites such as the temple, tabernacle, or other sanctuaries dedicated to Jehovah, but also can denote sanctuaries of idols or other nations. The top translations like 'of the sanctuary,' 'my sanctuary,' and 'the sanctuary' highlight its primary function as a designated dwelling place of God or a sacred refuge, underscoring its central role in worship and divine presence.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מִקְדָּשׁ as a consecrated, sanctified place enriches our grasp of God's desire to dwell among His people in holiness. It reflects God's initiative in setting apart a physical space where His presence is uniquely manifest and where covenant relationship is cultivated. For the Christian faith, this points forward to Christ as the ultimate sanctuary—God incarnate who sanctifies and dwells with humanity. The concept of a miqdâsh also reminds believers of the call to holiness and separation unto God, both corporately and individually, as a living temple of His Spirit.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 15:17 speaks of God bringing His people to dwell in the 'Sanctuary' He has prepared, emphasizing the miqdâsh as a divinely established place of inheritance and presence. The word 'Sanctuary' here conveys more than a location; it is a hallowed space crafted by God's own hands for intimate fellowship. This highlights the miqdâsh as God's intentional dwelling among His people, a theme that resonates throughout Scripture and invites believers to recognize God’s provision of a sacred place for communion and worship.
